newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds keep up pressure on US spread.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds keep up pressure on US spread.

text.p: Australian bond yields fell sharply as fresh calls for a monetary policy easing gathered pace and put further downward pressure on spreads to the U.S.
The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread narrowed to its lowest level in over 2-1/4 years, following through Wednesday's trend when it broke through the psycholocial 100 basis points barrier.

The latest move followed data showing just a 0.7 percent rise in August quarter average weekly earnings, and combined with Wednesday's annual underlying inflation rate falling to 2.4 percent, a 1/2 point rate cut has been priced in the market.
The spread tightening to the U.S. occured despite U.S. Treasuries firming after this week's note supply was absorbed.

The local market also outpaced the the Canadian market, which while stronger on Wednesday, showed some disappointment that the Bank of Canada did not ease policy as had been expected after a subdued Canadian CPI earlier in the week.

Meanwhile, local bonds kept near enough in tandem with a renewed advance in New Zealand bonds, with yields there also falling sharply after the RBNZ said that monetary conditions were tighter than necessary.
